questions.prompt: What grammatical structure is required at the beginning of the sentence?
options: A noun phrase functioning as the subject
A past participle forming a passive verb
A conjunction linking two complete clauses
questions.answer: A noun phrase functioning as the subject
questions.explanation: The sentence needs a person or role as its subject; a noun phrase such as “manager” can be followed by the modifier “responsible for…”.

questions.context: The shipment was held at customs [1] the accompanying certificate did not include the manufacturer's address.
questions.prompt: Which connector is needed before the clause?
options: A subordinating conjunction introducing a cause
A transition used only between two independent sentences
A preposition followed by a noun phrase
questions.answer: A subordinating conjunction introducing a cause
questions.explanation: The missing information explains the reason for the shipment being held, so “because” introduces the cause clause.

questions.context: The training center [1] the regional managers meet is located beside the airport.
questions.prompt: Which word introduces the place-related clause?
options: A relative adverb referring to a location
A relative pronoun referring to a person
An indefinite pronoun referring to a number
questions.answer: A relative adverb referring to a location
questions.explanation: The clause identifies the place where the managers meet; “where” introduces a location-related relative clause.

questions.context: By the time the auditors arrive, the accounting team [1] the supporting records.
questions.prompt: Which tense/aspect is required to show completion before a future point?
questions.explanation: The phrase “By the time…arrive” sets a future deadline; the future perfect (“will have organized”) shows the records will be ready before it.

questions.context: The company [1] its online returns process twice since January.
questions.prompt: Which verb tense is required with “since January” and a continuing time period up to now?
questions.explanation: The change has happened during a period that began in the past and continues to the present, so the present perfect is appropriate.

questions.context: The inspection team completed the review ahead of schedule. [1] As a result, the facility can reopen a day earlier than planned.
questions.prompt: What type of sentence would best fill blank [1]?
options: A complete sentence explaining the practical outcome of the early completion
A fragment naming an unrelated piece of equipment
A sentence that contradicts the early completion
A greeting addressed to the inspection team
questions.answer: A complete sentence explaining the practical outcome of the early completion
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins “As a result,” so the gap should establish a relevant consequence that makes the reopening possible.

questions.context: The final contract was [1] by the legal department before it was sent to the client.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the passive construction requires a past participle?
questions.explanation: “Was” in this passive structure must be followed by a past participle; “review” is the base form.

questions.context: Please submit the completed application [1] so that processing can begin without delay.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the blank needs an adverb describing how the application is submitted?
questions.explanation: “Accurate” is an adjective and cannot modify the verb “submit” in this position; the other choices function as adverbs.

questions.context: The orientation session will take place [1] Thursday afternoon in Room 208.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it is not used before a day of the week in this time expression?
questions.explanation: The standard expressions are “on Thursday,” “this Thursday” and “next Thursday”; “at Thursday” is incorrect.

questions.context: The shipment will be released [1] the customs documents have been approved.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it cannot introduce the finite clause that follows?
questions.explanation: “Despite” is a preposition and must be followed by a noun phrase or gerund, not a subject–verb clause.

questions.context: The accounting team has [1] the quarterly figures to the management board.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the present-perfect structure requires a past participle?
questions.explanation: After “has,” the main verb must be in the past-participle form; “present” is the base form.

questions.context: Each of the regional offices [1] a separate monthly inventory report.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the singular subject “Each” requires a singular verb?
questions.explanation: “Each” is grammatically singular, so the verb needs the -s form in the present simple.

questions.context: Employees are encouraged to [1] their passwords every 90 days to protect their accounts.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the infinitive marker “to” must be followed by the base form of a verb?
questions.explanation: The infinitive marker “to” is followed by a base-form verb; “updating” is a gerund or present participle.

questions.context: The orientation session is scheduled [1] the entire period from 2:00 p.m. until 4:00 p.m.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it cannot be used before the noun phrase “the entire period”?
questions.explanation: “Throughout,” “during” and “for” can introduce the period; “between” requires two endpoints, not the singular noun phrase “the entire period.”

questions.context: The manager asked the assistant [1] the revised schedule to all department heads.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the verb pattern is “ask someone to do something”?
questions.explanation: After “asked the assistant,” this instruction requires a to-infinitive; the gerund “sending” does not fit the pattern.

questions.context: Employees are encouraged to [1] their passwords regularly as part of the security policy.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the infinitive marker “to” must be followed by the base form of a verb?
questions.explanation: The infinitive marker “to” is followed by a base-form verb; “updating” is a gerund or present participle.

questions.context: The supplier agreed to [1] the delivery deadline after the warehouse requested an additional day.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it does not collocate with “deadline” in this meaning?
questions.explanation: A deadline can be extended, met or moved, but “enlarge a deadline” is not the standard collocation.

questions.context: Customers can [1] a refund by completing the online request form.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it does not mean formally asking to receive a refund?
questions.explanation: Customers may request, apply for or claim a refund; “borrow a refund” does not express this meaning.

questions.context: The technician will [1] an inspection of the ventilation system before reopening the laboratory.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it is not used with the noun “inspection” in this expression?
questions.explanation: A technician may conduct, carry out or perform an inspection; “lend an inspection” is not a valid verb–noun collocation.

questions.context: The revised instructions are intended to [1] confusion among first-time users.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it expresses the opposite of the intended meaning?
questions.explanation: The sentence states that the instructions are intended to make the process clearer, so “increase” contradicts the purpose.

questions.context: The revised handbook contains a new section on travel reimbursement. [1], it includes a glossary of common expense categories for staff members.
questions.prompt: Which transition should be eliminated because it incorrectly presents the glossary as a direct consequence of the new section?
questions.explanation: The glossary is another feature included in the handbook, not a consequence caused by the reimbursement section. An additive transition is appropriate.

questions.context: The director postponed the announcement [1] the final figures had not yet been confirmed.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the blank introduces a reason clause?
questions.explanation: “Although” introduces a contrast or concession, not the reason for postponing the announcement.

questions.context: The warehouse supervisor asked the driver to [1] the damaged cartons from the undamaged ones.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it does not mean to identify differences or keep items apart?
questions.explanation: The task is to keep damaged cartons apart from the others; “combine” means to put them together and contradicts the instruction.

questions.context: The new accounting software is compatible [1] the company's existing payroll system.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it is not the preposition used after “compatible”?
questions.explanation: The standard construction is “compatible with”; “compatible to” is not correct in this context.

questions.context: The team leader thanked everyone for responding [1] to the emergency procedure.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it has a negative meaning that conflicts with the appreciation expressed?
questions.explanation: The sentence praises the team's response, so “carelessly” contradicts the positive evaluation.

questions.context: The company introduced a secure portal [1] suppliers can upload their invoices.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because the blank refers to a place or system in which an action occurs?
questions.explanation: “That” alone does not express the required location relationship; “where” or a prepositional relative phrase would fit.

questions.context: The training materials were revised last week. [1] have been uploaded to the employee portal for immediate use.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it does not agree with the plural antecedent “materials”?
questions.explanation: “It” is singular, while the antecedent “materials” is plural; a plural pronoun or noun phrase is required.

questions.context: The revised employee handbook contains a new section on travel reimbursement. [1], it includes a glossary of common expense categories for staff members.
questions.prompt: Which transition should be eliminated because it incorrectly presents the glossary as a direct consequence of the new section?
questions.explanation: The glossary is an additional feature of the handbook, not a result caused by the reimbursement section. An additive transition is appropriate.

questions.context: The new warehouse uses automated sorting equipment. [1] This allows orders to be prepared more quickly during peak periods.
questions.prompt: Which sentence should be eliminated because it introduces an unrelated topic rather than explaining the equipment's benefit?
options: The system directs parcels to the correct dispatch area.
The equipment also records the movement of each package.
The company cafeteria will introduce a new menu on Monday.
Staff can identify delays from the live dashboard.
questions.answer: The company cafeteria will introduce a new menu on Monday.
questions.explanation: The other sentences explain functions or benefits of the sorting system; the cafeteria announcement breaks the topic.

questions.context: The service contract expires on 31 December. [1] To avoid an interruption, clients should submit renewal requests by 15 December.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it conflicts with the stated expiry date?
options: The current agreement will remain valid through the end of December.
The service will continue under the existing terms until the expiry date.
The contract ended several months ago and can no longer be renewed.
Clients should confirm any changes to their contact details.
questions.answer: The contract ended several months ago and can no longer be renewed.
questions.explanation: The passage says the contract expires in the future, so a sentence claiming it ended months ago contradicts the timeline.

questions.context: The new branch is located near the central station. [1] Customers can reach it easily by bus or train.
questions.prompt: Which sentence should be eliminated because it introduces information unrelated to the branch's location or accessibility?
options: A pedestrian bridge connects it to the station entrance.
The office is on the ground floor of the transit plaza.
The nearest bus stop is directly across the street.
The company's founding team met in a different city.
questions.answer: The company's founding team met in a different city.
questions.explanation: The first three sentences add details about the branch's location or access; the founding team's history does not develop that topic.

questions.context: The audit team will complete its final checks by noon. [1], the finance director will present the findings at 3:00 p.m.
questions.prompt: Which transition should be eliminated because it incorrectly suggests the presentation takes place while the checks are still in progress?
questions.explanation: The presentation is scheduled after the checks have been completed; “Meanwhile” signals simultaneous activity.

questions.context: The applicant submitted a portfolio and two references. [1] were checked by the recruitment team before the interview.
questions.prompt: Which option should be eliminated because it refers only to one item rather than all the plural materials?
questions.explanation: The plural portfolio-and-references group is referred to by “They,” “Both” or “The documents”; singular “It” does not agree.

questions.context: The store has extended its return period to 45 days. [1] Customers must still provide proof of purchase when requesting an exchange.
questions.prompt: Which sentence should be eliminated because it would contradict the extended return policy?
options: Items may be returned within 45 days of purchase.
The revised period gives customers more time to make a decision.
All returns must be requested within seven days of purchase.
The new policy applies to purchases made from 1 June.
questions.answer: All returns must be requested within seven days of purchase.
questions.explanation: A seven-day limit contradicts the stated 45-day return period.

questions.context: The supplier has confirmed that the spare parts are in stock. [1] The maintenance team can now schedule the repair.
questions.prompt: Which transition should be eliminated because it signals contrast rather than a logical next step?
questions.explanation: The stock confirmation enables the repair to be scheduled, so a result or consequence transition is needed rather than a contrast marker.

questions.context: The customer requested an updated delivery estimate. [1] The support agent checked the carrier's tracking system and replied with a revised arrival date.
questions.prompt: Which sentence should be eliminated because it interrupts the logical sequence of the request and response?
options: The carrier had reported a delay at the regional sorting center.
The parcel was expected to reach the customer two days later.
The company's annual staff awards will be held in December.
The customer was advised to use the tracking number for future updates.

questions.explanation: The other sentences develop the delivery inquiry and its response; the staff awards announcement is unrelated.
